title: Unilateral Declaration of Independence and Mayotte Sovereignty Dispute
description: On July 6, 1975, the Comorian Chamber of Deputies under Ahmed Abdallah unilaterally declared independence from France for the four-island archipelago after a 1974 referendum showed overall approval. France recognised independence for Grande Comore, Anjouan and Moheli but invoked island-by-island counts to retain Mayotte, which had voted overwhelmingly to stay French, opening a sovereignty dispute that the UN General Assembly has condemned annually ever since.

title: Mayotte Sovereignty Claim Lodged at the United Nations
description: Within months of independence, Comoros lodged its claim over Mayotte at the United Nations, framing France's retention of the island as a violation of territorial integrity and the OAU principle of inherited colonial borders. The UN General Assembly accepted Comoros within its 1975 borders and has reaffirmed the claim repeatedly, though France has never withdrawn and Mayotte became a French department in 2011.

title: First Bob Denard Coup Ousts Ahmed Abdallah
description: On August 3, 1975, only weeks after independence, French mercenary Bob Denard led a small armed force that overthrew President Ahmed Abdallah in a near-bloodless coup, installing a council that brought the radical young leader Ali Soilih to power. The episode set the template for three decades in which Denard and his soldiers would repeatedly decide who ruled the islands.

title: Ali Soilih's Maoist-Inspired Revolutionary Government
description: Ali Soilih consolidated power in early 1976 and launched a radical socialist programme inspired by Maoist and Tanzanian models, dissolving the civil service, lowering the voting age to fourteen and burning state archives. His youth militias and anti-clerical campaign in the deeply Muslim society alienated traditional notables and merchants and pushed the country toward economic collapse.

title: France Cuts Aid and Withdraws Technical Assistance
description: In response to Soilih's confrontational stance and the Mayotte dispute, France cut development aid and withdrew most of the French civil servants who had run the colonial administration, leaving Comoros with almost no trained personnel. The shock collapse of budget support deepened the country's structural dependence on external donors that has persisted ever since.

title: Karthala Volcanic Eruption Destroys Singani Village
description: Mount Karthala on Grande Comore erupted in 1977, with a lava flow destroying much of the village of Singani and displacing several thousand inhabitants. The eruption underlined the chronic exposure of the most populated island to one of the most active volcanoes in the Indian Ocean and the limited capacity of the new state to manage natural hazards.

title: Second Denard Coup Restores Ahmed Abdallah
description: On May 13, 1978, Bob Denard returned with about fifty mercenaries, killed Ali Soilih and reinstalled Ahmed Abdallah and Mohamed Ahmed as co-presidents, ending the revolutionary regime. Denard converted to Islam, took the name Said Mustapha Mahdjoub and remained as commander of the Presidential Guard, embedding mercenary control over the security apparatus for the next eleven years.

title: New Federal Constitution Establishing Islamic Republic
description: A referendum in October 1978 approved a new constitution that re-established Comoros as a Federal Islamic Republic, restored ties with conservative Arab and Western states and confirmed Abdallah as president. The text formally recognised three constituent islands while leaving Mayotte's seat vacant, and centralised power in the federal presidency.

title: Comoros Joins the Arab League
description: Comoros joined the Arab League in 1979, deepening political and financial ties with Gulf states and consolidating its identity as the smallest and only sub-equatorial member of the bloc. Membership opened a steady channel of Saudi, Emirati and Kuwaiti aid that became central to the federal budget and to mosque construction across the islands.

title: Single-Party Rule Under the Comorian Union for Progress
description: Abdallah's regime amended the constitution to establish the Comorian Union for Progress as the sole legal party and held single-list legislative elections. Political pluralism was suspended for the rest of the decade, opposition leaders were forced into exile in France and arbitrary detentions of dissidents became routine.

title: Abdallah Re-elected Unopposed in Single-Candidate Vote
description: President Ahmed Abdallah was re-elected for a second six-year term in September 1984 in a single-candidate referendum officially recording over 99 percent approval. The vote consolidated personal rule, with Bob Denard's Presidential Guard and a small inner circle of relatives controlling state contracts and security.

title: Failed Coup Attempt by Comorian Soldiers Against Denard's Guard
description: In March 1985, a group of Comorian soldiers and civilian opposition figures attempted to seize power and dismantle Denard's Presidential Guard, but the plot was crushed within hours. Mass arrests followed and Amnesty International documented torture of detainees, deepening international concern about the mercenary-backed security state.

title: Second Failed Coup Attempt and Renewed Crackdown
description: A further coup attempt in November 1987, partly led by exiled opposition figures and disaffected officers, was put down by the Presidential Guard with several deaths and dozens of arrests. The government accused South African and Belgian backers of involvement, and the episode reinforced Abdallah's reliance on Denard at the expense of the regular army.

title: Assassination of Ahmed Abdallah and Third Denard Coup
description: On November 26, 1989, President Ahmed Abdallah was shot dead in his office in circumstances pointing to Denard's Presidential Guard. Denard briefly took control of the country before French and South African pressure, including a deal that flew him to South Africa, ended his rule, marking the third Comorian coup directly tied to him.

title: Said Mohamed Djohar Wins First Multi-Candidate Election
description: Following Abdallah's killing, an interim government organised the country's first competitive presidential election in March 1990, won by Supreme Court chief Said Mohamed Djohar against Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim. The vote opened a fragile period of multi-party politics with frequent prime ministerial changes and contested legislative results.

title: New Multi-Party Constitution Approved by Referendum
description: Voters approved a new constitution in June 1992 that explicitly authorised political parties, separated executive and legislative powers and reinforced the federal structure of the three islands. Implementation was undermined almost immediately by repeated dissolutions of parliament and constitutional crises between Djohar and his shifting coalitions.

title: Failed Coup Attempt by Djohar's Stepson
description: In September 1992, a group of officers including President Djohar's stepson Mohamed Said Abass attempted to seize the radio station and key government buildings in Moroni, but were defeated within hours. The episode highlighted personalised factional politics inside the elite and led to a wave of military trials.

title: Fourth Denard Coup and French Operation Azalee
description: On September 28, 1995, Bob Denard returned with about thirty mercenaries, captured President Djohar and seized Moroni in a fourth coup attempt. France launched Operation Azalee within days, landing six hundred paratroopers who arrested the mercenaries without combat, took Denard to France for trial and restored constitutional order.

title: Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim Elected President
description: In March 1996, conservative Islamist-leaning candidate Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim won the presidential election with strong support on Anjouan, succeeding the transitional administration that had replaced Djohar. Taki promised to fight corruption and reorient policy toward the Arab world but inherited an empty treasury and growing inter-island grievances.

title: Anjouan and Moheli Declare Secession from Comoros
description: On August 3, 1997, Anjouan declared independence under Abdallah Ibrahim, demanding either reattachment to France or full sovereignty over what islanders called systematic neglect by Moroni; Moheli followed with its own secessionist proclamation. The federal army's attempt to retake Anjouan in September was repelled with significant casualties, opening a six-year separatist crisis.

title: Sudden Death of President Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim
description: President Mohamed Taki Abdoulkarim died suddenly on November 6, 1998 of an officially reported heart attack, with persistent rumours of poisoning. Interim president Tadjidine Ben Said Massounde, an Anjouanais, took office under the constitution but was unable to resolve the secession crisis, leaving a power vacuum that the army would exploit.

title: Fifth Coup Brings Colonel Azali Assoumani to Power
description: On April 30, 1999, Colonel Azali Assoumani, chief of staff of the army, overthrew interim president Massounde, arguing that civilian leaders were incapable of resolving the Anjouan secession. The coup was condemned by the OAU and triggered sanctions, but Azali consolidated control and opened negotiations with Anjouan separatists under regional pressure.

title: Fomboni Agreement Establishes Rotating Presidency
description: Mediated by the OAU and South Africa, the Fomboni Agreement signed in February 2001 created a new Union of the Comoros with a federal presidency rotating every four years among the three islands and broad autonomy for each island's government. The deal ended the Anjouan secession crisis and was endorsed by referendum in December 2001.

title: New Constitution of the Union of the Comoros Approved
description: Voters approved a new constitution on December 23, 2001, formally creating the Union of the Comoros with three island presidents and a rotating union president. The text decentralised most powers to the islands, established complex revenue-sharing rules and locked in the rotation principle that would shape the next two decades of politics.

title: Azali Assoumani Wins First Union Presidential Election
description: In April 2002, Colonel Azali won the first presidential election under the new union constitution after the leading civilian challenger withdrew citing irregularities. The result confirmed the army's tutelage over the political transition while installing the rotation principle that mandated his successor come from a different island.

title: Beit Salam Accord Operationalises Power-Sharing
description: In December 2003, the Beit Salam Accord brokered by South Africa and the African Union finalised the practical division of competences between the Union and the three island governments, including security, customs and the central bank. Implementation was repeatedly delayed but the framework anchored the post-secession settlement.

title: Karthala Volcano Eruption Disrupts Grande Comore
description: Mount Karthala erupted in April 2005 with a major ash plume that contaminated water cisterns across Grande Comore and forced over forty thousand people to evacuate. The eruption triggered an international humanitarian response and exposed the chronic absence of safe alternative water supplies on the most populous island.

title: Sufi Cleric Ahmed Abdallah Sambi Elected President
description: In May 2006, Anjouan-born Sufi cleric Ahmed Abdallah Mohamed Sambi, educated in Iran and Sudan, won the union presidential election as the rotation passed to Anjouan, defeating two military-backed candidates. The transition was the first peaceful handover between elected presidents in Comorian history and was hailed by the AU as a democratic milestone.

title: Karthala Eruption Repeats Water Crisis on Grande Comore
description: A second significant Karthala eruption in May 2006 again contaminated rainwater cisterns that supply most households on Grande Comore, requiring emergency water trucking by the Red Cross and Comorian authorities. The repeated disruption underlined the structural water vulnerability of the capital island.

title: Mohamed Bacar Holds Unconstitutional Election on Anjouan
description: In June 2007, Anjouan island president Mohamed Bacar organised an island presidential election in defiance of the Union government and the African Union, declaring himself re-elected. The AU and SADC condemned the vote as illegal and imposed targeted sanctions, opening a year-long standoff between Moroni and Mutsamudu.

title: Karthala Eruption Continues Volcanic Cycle
description: Karthala erupted again in January 2007, the third significant event in three years, with localised ashfall and renewed cistern contamination on Grande Comore. The recurring activity prompted the installation of a permanent volcano observatory with French scientific support.

title: AU Operation Democracy Removes Mohamed Bacar from Anjouan
description: On March 25, 2008, an African Union force led by Tanzania, Sudan and Senegal landed on Anjouan with logistical support from France and Libya, ousting Mohamed Bacar within twenty-four hours in Operation Democracy in Comoros. Bacar fled by speedboat to Mayotte and ultimately to Benin, restoring federal authority on the island.

title: Citizenship-by-Investment Programme with Gulf States Begins
description: The Sambi government formally launched a citizenship-by-investment programme aimed at selling Comorian passports to stateless bidoon residents of Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates in exchange for substantial fees. The scheme generated tens of millions of dollars off-budget and would later be denounced by parliament as the largest corruption scandal in the country's history.

title: Constitutional Referendum Postpones Rotation Schedule
description: In May 2009, voters approved constitutional amendments that extended the union presidential term from four to five years and synchronised island and union institutions, effectively prolonging Sambi's mandate. Opposition parties denounced the amendments as a manipulation of the rotation principle, foreshadowing recurring constitutional engineering by sitting presidents.

title: Yemenia Flight 626 Crashes off Grande Comore Killing 152
description: On June 30, 2009, Yemenia Airways Flight 626 from Sanaa crashed into the Indian Ocean during landing approach at Moroni, killing 152 of the 153 people on board, most of them Comorians returning home. The disaster prompted European bans on Yemenia and a long civil suit by victims' families that exposed weaknesses in airline oversight.

title: Ikililou Dhoinine Elected President from Moheli
description: In December 2010, vice president and pharmacist Ikililou Dhoinine won the union presidential election, becoming the first head of state from Moheli under the rotation. The orderly handover from Sambi to Dhoinine was widely viewed as a consolidation of constitutional politics, despite low turnout and limited campaign funding.

title: France Departmentalises Mayotte Deepening Sovereignty Dispute
description: On March 31, 2011, Mayotte officially became the 101st French department after a 2009 referendum, with full integration into the French and EU legal order. Comoros immediately protested that the move violated UN resolutions on its territorial integrity and continued to insist that Mayotte remained legally part of the Union of the Comoros.

title: Mass Migration Crisis on the Mayotte Sea Route
description: Through the early 2010s, thousands of Comorians attempted the dangerous thirty-mile crossing from Anjouan to Mayotte each year on small kwassa-kwassa boats, with estimates of seven to ten thousand deaths since the 1995 introduction of the Balladur visa. By 2012 the route had become one of the deadliest internal migration corridors in the world.

title: Friendship Treaty with France Reactivates Bilateral Cooperation
description: Comoros and France signed a Declaration of Paris in June 2013 reactivating bilateral cooperation, opening a high-level joint commission on Mayotte and committing to development financing. The accord did not resolve the sovereignty dispute but stabilised the relationship and unlocked Agence Francaise de Developpement programmes.

title: Citizenship-by-Investment Scandal Exposed by Parliament
description: A 2015 parliamentary inquiry concluded that some 48,000 Comorian passports had been sold to Gulf bidoon between 2008 and 2014 for an estimated 200 million dollars, only a small fraction of which entered the state budget. Former president Sambi was named as the principal beneficiary, opening a legal saga that would lead to his prosecution years later.

title: Azali Assoumani Returns to the Presidency
description: In a contested three-round election concluded in May 2016, former coup leader Colonel Azali Assoumani won the union presidency as the rotation returned to Grande Comore, narrowly defeating opposition candidate Mohamed Ali Soilihi. Opposition rejected the official result citing irregularities on Anjouan but the constitutional court confirmed the outcome.

title: African Development Bank Country Strategy Targets Energy and Roads
description: The African Development Bank approved a new country strategy paper for Comoros in 2017 prioritising electricity generation on Anjouan and road rehabilitation on Grande Comore as preconditions for private investment. Chronic blackouts had crippled the SONELEC utility and the strategy framed energy reform as the binding constraint on growth.

title: Constitutional Referendum Ends the Rotating Presidency
description: On July 30, 2018, a referendum boycotted by most opposition parties officially approved by 92 percent a new constitution scrapping the rotating presidency, extending presidential terms and allowing Azali to seek two more consecutive five-year mandates. The OIF and AU expressed concern at the contested process, opening a deep legitimacy crisis.

title: Anjouan Uprising and Violent Crackdown in Mutsamudu
description: In October 2018, a military mutiny by armed opposition supporters in the historic medina of Mutsamudu on Anjouan was crushed by the federal army using armoured vehicles and helicopters over several days, killing several people. Mass arrests followed and human rights groups documented torture of detainees, deepening tensions on the island.

title: Azali Re-Elected in First Round Amid Fraud Allegations
description: On March 24, 2019, Colonel Azali was officially re-elected in the first round with 60.8 percent of the vote, a result rejected by all twelve opposition candidates and observed by the AU and OIF as marred by serious irregularities. Protests erupted in Moroni and a brief armed standoff at military camps was put down within hours.

title: Cyclone Kenneth Devastates Northern Comoros
description: On April 25, 2019, Cyclone Kenneth, the strongest cyclone ever recorded to make landfall in Comoros, struck the northern islands with category 4 winds, killing seven people and damaging or destroying nearly half of all homes on Anjouan and parts of Grande Comore. The storm caused damages estimated at 185 million dollars, around 12 percent of GDP.

title: Geneva Donors Conference Pledges 4.3 Billion for Recovery
description: In December 2019, a Comoros partners conference in Geneva co-hosted by the World Bank and the AU mobilised 4.3 billion dollars in pledges over five years to fund post-Kenneth reconstruction and the government's emerging plan. Actual disbursements over the following years fell well short of the headline figure but the pledge anchored a new donor framework.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Reaches the Archipelago
description: The first COVID-19 cases were officially confirmed in Comoros on April 30, 2020, prompting curfews, mosque closures and a halt to passenger flights that severely disrupted the diaspora-dependent economy. The death of Vice President Djaffar Said Ahmed Hassani in July 2020, attributed to COVID-19, dramatised the human cost on the political elite.

title: Sambi Sentenced to Life for High Treason in Passport Scandal
description: On November 30, 2021, the State Security Court sentenced former president Ahmed Abdallah Sambi to life imprisonment for high treason in connection with the citizenship-by-investment scandal, ending three years of pre-trial detention. Opposition figures and the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention denounced the trial as politically motivated.

title: Comoros Assumes Chairmanship of the African Union
description: President Azali Assoumani took over the rotating chairmanship of the African Union for 2023 at the February 2023 summit, with Comoros formally elected the previous year. The role gave the smallest African state by population a year of unprecedented diplomatic visibility, though critics said it deflected attention from domestic governance problems.

title: IMF Extended Credit Facility Anchors Reform Programme
description: The IMF approved a 43 million dollar four-year Extended Credit Facility for Comoros in June 2023, supporting fiscal reforms, central bank governance changes and energy sector restructuring. The programme followed years of stalled engagement and aimed to consolidate post-pandemic recovery and channel donor financing.

title: France Launches Operation Wuambushu to Expel Migrants from Mayotte
description: From April 2023, French authorities launched Operation Wuambushu on Mayotte to demolish slums and deport thousands of Comorian migrants back to Anjouan, prompting Comoros to refuse landing of repatriation boats for several weeks. The operation triggered the worst diplomatic rupture in years and revived the territorial dispute.

title: January 2024 Attempted Attack on Beit-Salam Presidential Palace
description: On January 7, 2024, gunmen attacked the Beit-Salam presidential palace in Moroni in what authorities described as an attempted coup, with several attackers killed and dozens arrested. The incident, days before the presidential campaign opened, highlighted the fragility of security around Azali's contested third term.

title: Azali Re-Elected for Fourth Term in Boycotted Vote
description: On January 14, 2024, Azali Assoumani was declared re-elected in the first round with 63 percent on a turnout officially recorded at only 16 percent, after most opposition parties boycotted. The election commission's results were rejected by the main opposition coalition and by independent observers as lacking credibility.

title: Post-Election Riots Across Grande Comore and Anjouan
description: Following the announcement of Azali's victory, days of rioting erupted across Moroni, Mutsamudu and other towns in mid-January 2024, with at least one person killed, government buildings burned and a nighttime curfew imposed. Internet was throttled and dozens were arrested in what became the most serious civil unrest since 2018.

title: Cholera Outbreak Spreads from Anjouan
description: A cholera outbreak that began in February 2024 on Anjouan spread to Grande Comore and Moheli within weeks, with the World Health Organization recording several thousand cases and dozens of deaths by mid-year. The epidemic strained the under-resourced health system already weakened by years of fiscal austerity.

title: Cyclone Chido Brushes Comoros Before Devastating Mayotte
description: On December 14, 2024, Cyclone Chido passed close to Comoros causing severe damage on Moheli and parts of Anjouan before making catastrophic landfall on French Mayotte. The storm renewed cross-strait humanitarian and political tensions, with Comorian authorities offering assistance and reasserting their sovereignty claim.

title: Legislative Elections Reinforce Ruling Party Dominance
description: Legislative elections held in January 2025 were again boycotted by the main opposition, delivering an overwhelming majority to Azali's Convention for the Renewal of the Comoros and allied independents. International observation was minimal and the new assembly was widely viewed as a rubber stamp for the executive.

title: Vanilla and Ylang-Ylang Export Crisis Hits Rural Incomes
description: Through 2024 and into 2025, Comorian vanilla and ylang-ylang producers, who supply a significant share of world ylang oil for the perfume industry, faced collapsed prices driven by Madagascan oversupply and synthetic substitutes, sharply reducing rural cash incomes on Anjouan and Moheli. The shock deepened food insecurity and out-migration pressures.

title: Energy Sector Reform and Grid Investments Continue
description: Under the IMF programme, the government in 2025 advanced restructuring of the SONELEC utility and accelerated implementation of solar and hybrid generation projects co-financed by the AfDB and Abu Dhabi Fund. Persistent blackouts on Anjouan continued to provoke local protests despite tariff reforms aimed at financial sustainability.

title: UN General Assembly Reaffirms Mayotte Sovereignty Resolution
description: The UN General Assembly in 2025 again adopted, with overwhelming support from non-Western blocs, the annual resolution reaffirming Comorian sovereignty over Mayotte and calling for negotiations between Paris and Moroni. France continued to vote against and to administer Mayotte as an integral part of the Republic, leaving the dispute frozen.
